what: A scroll-linked pass-by line sweeps from outside the left of the heading to outside the right. Letters the line head has passed are pushed and fall over a distance of 140px — ±50px sideways, 60~220px down (accelerating) — rotating ±80° and vanishing. If there is a flying object such as a paper plane (flyer), it flies along a wave path curving upward following the line head, and the letters where the plane passed scatter.

options.reach: Distance (px) until the letters fully scatter behind the leading edge of the line, default 140
options.wave: Height the flyer curves upward (share of heading height), default .75
options.track: (if present) measures the nearest ancestor found with this css — for when the title sits inside a screen-fixed panel

use: To the reader, the message is the product
note: In the original, a three.js 3D paper airplane flies over a screen-fixed title and scatters the letters. The part accepts the plane as any element (flyer) and sets its path as a wave relative to the title box — if 3D is needed, the user places a canvas in the flyer slot. The letter-scatter values (140px·±50·60~220·±80°·fade over a 1.15 share) match the copy’s index.js. Scrolling back up returns the letters to their places.

from.where: index.html .tw-pain__title — during the pinned range 4~38%, a plane flies from outside the title’s top left to outside the right, scattering the letters it has passed (copy index.js paint)
